subject.title: Feature: Telegram Reactions - Two-Way Support with Prompt Guidance

question: Should incoming reaction interpretation be folded into the existing `reactionLevel` contract and gated by `reactionNotifications`, or should Telegram gain a separate public `reactionGuidance` setting?
rationale: Both designs are implementable, but choosing configuration ownership, precedence, defaults, and separation from reaction-triggered execution is a public product and upgrade contract.

options.title: Extend reactionLevel
options.body: Keep one reaction-policy setting, add notification-aware incoming soft-signal guidance to its minimal and extensive modes, and avoid a parallel config source.

options.title: Add reactionGuidance
options.body: Introduce a separate off/minimal/full setting with explicit precedence, migration, schema, metadata, documentation, and tests against reactionLevel and reactionNotifications.

options.title: Defer incoming semantics
options.body: Keep current outbound-only guidance and leave reaction interpretation to the broader reaction-control design tracked in related issues.

recommendation.title: Extend reactionLevel
recommendation.body: Keep one reaction-policy setting, add notification-aware incoming soft-signal guidance to its minimal and extensive modes, and avoid a parallel config source.
